title: Redline an indemnification clause
instructions: You are counsel to the buyer (Kestrel Systems) in a software acquisition. The target's form SPA contains a one-way indemnification clause with no cap. Produce (1) a redline of the clause making the indemnity mutual, adding a basket and a cap at 15% of purchase price, and carving out fraud, IP infringement, and breach of confidentiality obligations from the cap, and (2) a one-sentence negotiation rationale for each change.

inputs.name: spa-excerpt.pdf
inputs.description: Section 9 (Indemnification) of the target's form SPA, 3 pages.

inputs.name: buyer-positions.md
inputs.description: Kestrel's approved indemnity positions and fallbacks.

sample_answer:
INDEMNIFICATION — PROPOSED REDLINE (Section 9)

9.1 Mutual Indemnity. [INSERT: 'Each of Buyer and the Target shall indemnify the other'] against Losses arising from (a) breach of this Agreement by the indemnifying party, and (b) fraud.

9.2 Cap. The indemnifying party's aggregate liability shall not exceed fifteen percent (15%) of the Purchase Price. Rationale: playbook position — cap sized to deal risk.

9.3 Carve-outs. The cap does not apply to (a) fraud, (b) infringement of intellectual property rights, or (c) breach of confidentiality obligations. Rationale: carve-outs track items where damages are hardest to bound.

Note: threshold mechanics to follow in the next draft.

contains_any: each of buyer and the target

rubric.criterion: Adds a damages cap set at 15% of the purchase price
Carves out fraud, IP infringement, and confidentiality breaches from the cap
Adds a deductible/basket before indemnity claims are payable
Provides a one-sentence rationale tied to the playbook for each edit
Invents obligations that appear in neither the excerpt nor the playbook (penalty)
Each redline element is anchored to a quoted phrase from the source or playbook
Fabricates a quote that does not exist in the source documents (penalty)
